entities.summary:
Thomas Basin (1412–1491) was a French bishop of Lisieux and historian. As a prominent cleric of the Catholic Church, he played a crucial role in the development of the French Reformation and the subsequent religious turmoil of the 15th century. His most notable work, the 'Historia Ecclesiastica', provides valuable insights into the politics and theology of the time.

 Basin's significance extends beyond his literary output, as he was also a key figure in the establishment of the University of Lisieux, a hub for theological education and intellectual discourse.

 The French Reformation, which Basin helped shape, had far-reaching consequences for the Catholic Church and the development of Protestantism in Europe.

 Basin's legacy can be seen in the continued study and analysis of his historical works, which remain an essential part of understanding the complex religious and political landscape of 15th-century France.

 In a striking testament to his enduring influence, Basin's 'Historia Ecclesiastica' has been translated into multiple languages and continues to be studied by scholars today.
